packs.title: Water & Wonder
packs.promise: Explore Granada through palace water, market choices, a park poem and a small science experiment.

q.s: Find water moving, reflecting and helping a garden grow during your Alhambra visit.
st: Before entering, check your ticket’s included spaces, palace time and the day’s route notices.
Along that route, find one channel or fountain that carries water, and one surface that can hold a reflection.
In the Generalife, look from an open visitor path at the canal and planted beds of the Patio de la Acequia. Use the linked operator account to connect water with garden care.
Make a three-part record: place, role and one visible detail. A dry feature counts if you say it was dry; do not describe a reflection you did not see.

q.s: Compose an imaginary meal from three things offered at the market.
st: Browse an open public aisle without blocking shoppers.
Choose three foods offered by the stalls or on their displayed menus that could belong in one imaginary meal.
Give each a role in the meal: the main part, an accompaniment or a finish.
For one ingredient, record its displayed origin if there is one; otherwise write “origin not shown.” Give your meal a name of your own.

q.s: Make two predictions, try two exhibits and let the results surprise you.
st: In the Percepción gallery, choose two operating exhibits whose instructions and sensory effects suit you.
Before trying each one, predict what you will see or hear. A one-word guess is enough.
Use each exhibit as instructed, then compare the result with your prediction.
Save one prediction that held up and one that changed, if that happened. Two correct predictions count just as much.

packs.title: Realejo Rooms
packs.promise: Spend two afternoons among Realejo squares, old rooms and connected garden slopes.

q.s: Separate a surviving room, a later building and a garden story.
st: On the open visitor route, locate the surviving qubba, or reception hall.
Use the interpretation or linked operator account to distinguish the old hall from the later building around it.
Read how the earlier garden relates to the garden seen today; do not assume everything visible is medieval.
Make three evidence cards in a note: “I saw,” “the source explains” and “I still wonder.” Put one detail in each.

q.s: Make a tiny score from a repeated sound, a pause and a change.
st: Listen briefly for a repeated sound, then a pause and a sound that changes. If listening is unsuitable, use repeated shapes, a gap and a change in shape instead.
Choose a simple mark for each: perhaps dots, a space and a curved line.
Arrange those marks into a short score on paper or in a note. Written sound or shape words work too.
Follow your score once silently, then give it a title drawn from what you noticed.

q.s: Find two garden spaces and decide which details make them feel different.
st: Stay on the open garden paths and choose two spaces you can comfortably reach.
In each, find two things shaping your view: a path edge, planting, an opening, a wall or a water feature.
Give each space a mood word of your own, then connect that word to one detail you actually saw.
Choose which space you would return to for ten more minutes and explain why. A dry water feature still counts as a visible form.
